title: A Girl, a Lost Lamby, and a Talking Octopus: This Movie Brings Sculptures to Life!
summary:
Have you ever stared at a painting or a statue and wished it could move? Artist Dustin Yellin did. He makes giant glass sculptures filled with tiny painted figures. He calls them "frozen cinema" because they look like a movie paused in mid-action. Now, with a little help from AI (artificial intelligence, or computer brains that can create things), his art has come to life in a short film called "Goodnight Lamby."

The movie stars Yellin's real daughter, Zia, who plays a version of herself. When her stuffed animal Lamby goes missing, she dives inside one of her dad's sculptures to find it. The world inside is a wild, watery dreamscape—imagine an undersea kingdom made of collage. A talking octopus (voiced by comedian Chris Rock) guides her on the journey. Even actor Paul Rudd pops up as a version of Dustin.

To make the film, the team used Google Veo 3, a special AI tool. They gave the computer prompts, like "make the water ripple" or "make that cloud float," and it generated moving images. Then artists combined those bits with live-action footage of Zia. It's like making a digital puppet show!

Yellin says he's not worried about people who think AI art is cheating. "The world is full of bad art," he says, "whether it's made with paint or a computer. What matters is the idea." He just wanted to see his frozen cinema finally move. And thanks to this team-up, now we all can.
why_it_matters: This shows how new computer tools can make art interactive, like a video game, so one day you might step into your favorite painting just like Zia did.

background_read: Dustin Yellin (an American artist in Brooklyn) is famous for making huge glass blocks with hundreds of painted figures trapped inside, like a 3D collage.
The film uses Google Veo 3, a new AI video tool that turns text into moving images, which is part of a growing trend of artists using computers to expand their creative toolbox.
Chris Rock (a well-known comedian and actor) and Paul Rudd (the actor who plays Ant-Man) both lent their voices and talents to this short film, bridging the worlds of fine art and Hollywood.
Article_Structure: WHO: The film stars Zia (Dustin Yellin's real daughter), a talking octopus (voiced by Chris Rock), and a cameo by Paul Rudd playing a version of Dustin.
WHAT: A short film called 'Goodnight Lamby' where Zia jumps inside one of her dad's giant glass sculptures to find her lost stuffed animal, brought to life with the help of AI.
WHERE: The adventure takes place inside a wild, watery dreamscape inside a Yellin sculpture—an undersea collage kingdom.
WHY: Dustin Yellin wanted to finally see his 'frozen cinema' move and partnered with AI artists to turn his static art into a moving story for everyone.

perspectives.description: For artists like Yellin, AI is a fantastic new brush that can bring still sculptures to life and open up storytelling possibilities that were never possible before.
Some people feel that using AI to make art is like copying the work of others without real effort, and they fear it might replace human creativity in the future.
Many believe that the quality of the final idea matters more than the tool used, and that a strong creative vision can turn any medium—paint, glass, or AI code—into meaningful art.
